attempts.prompt:
Game VFX animation cel for a friendly colorful cartoon bubble puzzle game. One single top-to-bottom electrical discharge, in portrait 1:2 framing destined for 256 x 512 with a genuine fully transparent RGBA background. Pure, neutral WHITE ink only. The arc is thin enough to flank a wordmark and still read when displayed just 150 pixels high. Design by varying the thickness of a single continuous sharply kinked electric filament, asymmetric angular fissure rhythm. The main trunk has a small but substantial upper stroke, roughly 10–14px in a 256px canvas, natural swelling and pinching locally at angular elbows, becoming much finer toward a sharp needle tip below. The upper terminal enters from just above the top edge and extends down to practically the bottom edge. Main trunk should wander a little to either side of the vertical centerline and return, never travel diagonally across the entire frame. Keep the upper and lower anchors near x=128 of 256. The entire silhouette INCLUDING subsidiary branches fits inside a narrow centered vertical strip approximately 100–125 px wide of the 256 px canvas. Draw EXACTLY TWO or THREE subordinate short, fine forked-off strokes, irregularly spaced, each emerging from a different point of the main zigzag, tapered and fading via alpha at its own tip, no detached flecks or additional twigs. Edges are crisp clean, anti-aliased, simple cartoon electric cel, just an extremely thin localized semi-transparent white softness touching the core. White core with transparent clear space on both sides; no colored pixels, no black ink, no outline, no purple, no shadow, no bright background or broad bloom, no gray opaque matte, no texture, no sparks, no stars, no dots, no text. Not a thunderbolt icon, not a rigid five-segment line, not a realistic fractal lightning tree. One static frame, no grid or contact sheet.
B1. Strong initial discharge. Enter near 50% width. The upper quarter slips left in a short abrupt step, snaps right through a brief narrow triangular elbow, a longer oblique descends through the middle-left, then a small sharp counter-kink in the lower third and a long thin terminal near the center. Two side filaments: a small upper one toward right at about 22% height and a lower one down-left around 62%.
attempts.reason: Wide baked bloom obscured the branch tips at gameplay scale.

attempts.prompt:
Draw ONE hand-drawn animation cel of a vertical electrical fissure for a cartoon game's spell effect. Use a clean, UNLIT, FLAT WHITE SILHOUETTE on REAL transparent background. Only the cut-paper shape of the white core, like an inked anime effects cel. Sharp, not pillowy. No rendered light, shading, atmosphere or bloom, just clean antialiased edges; final compositing handles the light. A slender connected crooked tapered ribbon of white, with knife-edge CUSPED vertices that form little wedges at turns. Do not make a smooth neon line, or a thick Z icon, or fluffy airbrushed lightning. Draw a single narrow continuous irregular trunk, with changes of direction at different intervals and a little extra weight as it folds at a bend. At its top the trunk is visibly thick, below the middle it becomes much thinner, and it tapers to a razor-sharp needle at the very bottom. Two or three SIMPLE fine side spurs only, clearly thinner and shorter than the trunk, tapering away from their EXACT ATTACHMENT to the trunk. Visible, clean and readable when reduced to 150px high. Narrow and long composition: 256×512 vertical uncolored sprite, core runs from upper center to bottom center. Upper thickness about 13px at the 256px width, bottom thickness 1–2px. Keep the complete silhouette about 108–128px wide including both offshoots and 505–512px tall. Keep both extremities near the horizontal center. No bright or dark background, no radial halo, no stroke outlines, no shading inside the white, no stars, no sparks, no detached dots, no text, no diagram, no other elements. A single isolated vertical white shape, never a sheet or sequence diagram.
